title: The bug fixers

story: RH-1240 arrives in Jira, triaged into the frontend team: "Clearing the datasets search leaves the table empty." You type something in the search box, delete it again, and every dataset is gone until you reload. A bug fixer, the routine that takes triaged Bug tickets, picks it up within five minutes.

It would be easy to read the ticket, look at the search code, make a change that looks right and open a PR with a confident description. The reviewer would then have to trust the agent's story, because nothing shows that the change touches the bug that the user saw. A fix that nobody can check is a guess with good grammar.
hook.question: How does a bug fixer prove that it found the reported bug and that its change really fixes it?

p: A bug fixer, like every routine, is the same agent as Nova, our ticket-to-PR agent, started by a triaged Bug ticket instead of an assignment. Its first rule is to reproduce the bug before changing any code. Reproducing means making the bug happen on purpose, as a test that fails: for RH-1240, a test that clears the search and expects every dataset back. Published research systems that fix GitHub issues with a model, such as Agentless and SWE-agent, work the same way, because a failing test turns a vague report into a precise one.

Before that, a cheap triage step with Sonnet 5.5 at low effort checks whether the ticket is a duplicate of an open one, belongs to the right team, and how bad it is. Then the reproduction runs with Opus 5.5 at high effort. If the bug cannot be reproduced, that is a useful result too: the fixer comments on the ticket with the steps it tried, the seed data and commands it used, what is missing (a role, a data shape, a browser, the exact steps) and one specific question, and the run ends as handed_off. A failed reproduction written up well saves the next person an hour.

The proof is one test run twice, and the harness, our program in the VM that runs the agent's session, runs it, not the model. First on the base commit, the main commit the fix started from, with only the new test files copied in and the old code unchanged. The test must fail there. Then on the fix, where it must pass. A test that passes on the old code does not test the bug, however good it looks.

To have both versions side by side, the harness uses a git worktree: a second checkout of the same repo in another folder, at another commit. The fix stays in /work/fcp, the base goes to /work/base, the test files are copied across, and the same test command runs in both folders. The Stop hook, which runs when the agent says it is done, keeps sending the agent back to work until both results hold, and the PR shows both logs side by side.

notes.text: A second checkout at the base commit, next to the fix.
Only the test files go across. The source in /work/base stays as it was.
The new test on the old code: it must fail.
The same test on the fix: it must pass.
Failed on base, and not because the test could not even load.
The ends of both logs go into the PR as evidence.

p: There is one trap in "must fail on base". Suppose the fix adds a helper, normaliseSearch, and the new test imports it. On the base commit the helper does not exist, so the test fails with a SyntaxError before a single assertion runs. It failed, but it proved nothing about the bug: any test that imports a new name fails on old code. So the proof counts only a failure on behaviour, an assertion that saw the wrong result. A setup error sends the agent back to rewrite the test so it checks what the user sees, for example the rows that visibleRows returns.

Two more rules keep the fix small and owned. If the fix is more than a small, local change, the plan, with the root cause at file and line, goes to the ticket's owner with Approve, Change and Stop buttons, and the run waits. And when the PR opens, the ticket is assigned to the routine's owner with the PR link and the proof, so a person owns the bug again.

deeper.h: Go deeper: the flaky-test fixer's proof
p: A flaky test passes sometimes and fails sometimes, so "fails before, passes after" is not enough. The flaky-test fixer first runs the test's whole module again and again with Django's --shuffle option and a new seed each time, a number that fixes one random order of the tests, until it fails; the failing seed makes the failure repeatable. After the fix it must pass 50 times in a row with new seeds, including the seed that used to fail. Its charter forbids adding retries or sleeps, which would hide the flake instead of fixing it.

notes.text: Each run shuffles the test order with a new seed.
One failure stops the proof, with the seed that made it fail.

lab.title: Prove the fix
lab.goal: Reproduce a small bug with a failing test, prove with a git worktree that the test fails on the old code and passes on the fix, and catch a test that fails for the wrong reason.

guess.q: The fix adds a helper, normaliseSearch, and the new test imports it. On the base commit the test fails. Is the bug reproduced?

options.text: Yes, it failed on base and passes on the fix.
options.why: It failed with a SyntaxError, because the helper does not exist on base. That says nothing about the bug.

options.text: No, because it failed for a setup reason; the test must fail on an assertion about behaviour.
options.why: Only a failure on behaviour shows the test catches the bug the user saw.

options.text: No, because tests may never import from the code they test.
options.why: Tests import code all the time. The problem is importing something only the fix created.

follow.say: Make a tiny repo with the bug from RH-1240 and see it: a cleared search, which arrives as null, hides every row.
follow.do:
mkdir -p ~/academy-labs/g5-7/fcp/src && cd ~/academy-labs/g5-7/fcp
git init -q -b main && git config user.email lab@example.com && git config user.name Lab
cat > src/datasets.js <<'EOF'
export const visibleRows = (rows, search) =>
  rows.filter((row) => row.name.toLowerCase().includes(search?.toLowerCase()));
EOF
git add . && git commit -qm "datasets table with search"
node -e 'import("./src/datasets.js").then(({ visibleRows }) => console.log(visibleRows([{ name: "Knee MRI" }], null)))'

follow.say: Write the regression test and the fix on a branch, and see the test pass on the fix. That is only half of the proof.
Write the first proof script. It makes a worktree at the base commit, copies in only the test, and runs the test in both places.
follow.do:
cat > ../prove.sh <<'EOF'
# Prove a regression test: it must fail on the base commit and pass on the fix.
base=$(git merge-base main HEAD)
tests=$(git diff --name-only "$base" HEAD -- test/)
rm -rf /tmp/g5-7-base && git worktree add -q /tmp/g5-7-base "$base"
for t in $tests; do mkdir -p "/tmp/g5-7-base/$(dirname "$t")" && cp "$t" "/tmp/g5-7-base/$t"; done
if (cd /tmp/g5-7-base && node --test > /tmp/g5-7-base.log 2>&1); then before=passed; else before=failed; fi
if node --test > /tmp/g5-7-head.log 2>&1; then after=passed; else after=failed; fi
git worktree remove --force /tmp/g5-7-base
echo "on base with only the test: $before"; grep -m1 -E "AssertionError|SyntaxError|Error \[" /tmp/g5-7-base.log
echo "on the fix:                 $after"
EOF
bash ../prove.sh
follow.see:
on base with only the test: failed
  name: 'AssertionError'
on the fix:                 passed

follow.say: Now a fix whose test imports a new helper. Run the same proof and look at why it failed on base.
follow.see:
on base with only the test: failed
# SyntaxError: The requested module '../src/datasets.js' does not provide an export named 'normaliseSearch'
on the fix:                 passed

lab.build: Turn prove.sh into a real check that ends with exit code 0 only for a real proof. It must fail with a clear message in three cases: the test passes on base (it does not catch the bug), the base log shows a setup error (SyntaxError, ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND or ReferenceError), or the test fails on the fix. Otherwise print that the bug is reproduced and fixed. Run it on bugfix/RH-1240 and bugfix/setup. Then rewrite the test on bugfix/setup so it checks visibleRows instead of the helper, and run the proof again.
checks: On bugfix/RH-1240 the proof prints that the bug is reproduced and fixed, and echo $? prints 0.
On bugfix/setup it reports a setup reason with the SyntaxError line, and exits with 1.
After you rewrite the bugfix/setup test to assert on visibleRows(rows, null).length, the proof passes there too.
git worktree list shows only the main checkout after each run: the base worktree is removed.

solution.text:
# Prove a regression test: it must fail on the base commit, for a behaviour reason, and pass on the fix.
base=$(git merge-base main HEAD)
tests=$(git diff --name-only "$base" HEAD -- test/)
rm -rf /tmp/g5-7-base && git worktree add -q /tmp/g5-7-base "$base"
for t in $tests; do mkdir -p "/tmp/g5-7-base/$(dirname "$t")" && cp "$t" "/tmp/g5-7-base/$t"; done
(cd /tmp/g5-7-base && node --test > /tmp/g5-7-base.log 2>&1); base_code=$?
node --test > /tmp/g5-7-head.log 2>&1; head_code=$?
git worktree remove --force /tmp/g5-7-base
if [ $base_code -eq 0 ]; then echo "✘ the test passes without the fix: it does not catch the bug"; exit 1; fi
if grep -qE "SyntaxError|ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND|ReferenceError" /tmp/g5-7-base.log; then
  echo "✘ the test fails on base for a setup reason, not the bug:"; grep -m1 -E "SyntaxError|ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND|ReferenceError" /tmp/g5-7-base.log; exit 1
fi
if [ $head_code -ne 0 ]; then echo "✘ the test fails on the fix too"; exit 1; fi
echo "✔ fails on base with an assertion, passes on the fix: the bug is reproduced and fixed"

lab.fix: A teammate simplified the proof: it now runs the test only on the fix, "because CI runs it anyway". Write a test that cannot fail, such as assert.ok(true), commit it with a change to src/datasets.js, and see the simplified proof call it a fix. Explain what the run on the base commit adds that no run on the fix can.
explain: Why must the regression test fail on the base commit before the fix counts?
Why is a SyntaxError on base not a reproduction?
Why does the harness run the proof, and not the agent that wrote the fix?
lab.done: Your proof accepts the honest fix, rejects the test that fails for a setup reason, and leaves no worktree behind.

check.q: A bug fixer's new test passes on the base commit and on the fix. What does that mean?

options.text: The fix is proven, because the test passes
options.why: It also passes without the fix, so it does not check the bug at all.

options.text: The test does not catch the bug, so the proof fails and the agent must write a better test
options.why: A regression test must fail on the old code. Otherwise it proves nothing about the fix.

options.text: The bug was already fixed on main
options.why: Possible, but the run cannot know that from this result. It only knows the test is not a reproduction.

check.q: The bug fixer cannot make the bug happen, after trying three different paths. What is the right outcome?

options.text: Guess a fix from the ticket text and open a draft PR
options.why: Reproduce first is the rule. A fix nobody can check is a guess.

options.text: Keep trying the same steps until something fails
options.why: Retrying blind costs time and finds nothing new. A person can add the missing detail.

options.text: Comment on the ticket with the steps tried, the data used, what is missing and one question, and end as handed_off
options.why: A failed reproduction written up well is useful on its own.

check.q: Why does the proof copy only the test files into the base worktree?

options.text: So the new test runs against the old code, which is the only way to see it fail on the bug
options.why: If the fix came along too, the test would pass on base and prove nothing.

options.text: Because copying the source would be too slow
options.why: Speed is not the reason. The base must keep the old code by design.

options.text: Because git worktrees cannot hold source files
options.why: A worktree is a full checkout. The point is which version of the code it holds.

p: The shared flow is in the harness: triage on Sonnet 5.5 low with a structured answer, reproduction on Opus 5.5 high, a plan with file:line that waits on decidePlan when the fix is bigger than small and local, and harness/src/checks/prove-regression.ts, which the Stop hook checks before done. Bugs come from the Jira bug poll every 5 minutes as bugfix:RH-1240 on the ai-agents-bugfix queue; when the PR opens, the ticket is assigned to the routine owner.

The FE bug fixer (charter fe-bug-fixer, frontend/**, a full on-demand VM because it waits on people) reproduces on FCP Lab with seed data from TestDataCreator and writes Vitest or Playwright specs in the AGENTS.md style, with the QA agent's videos as proof. The BE bug fixer writes a failing Django test with CommonRhinoTestCase and the factories, adds a curl transcript for API bugs, and hands gRPC, auth and migration changes to the BE guild. The flaky-test fixer runs one run per test (flaky:fcp:<hash>), 1 slot, and proves 50 green runs.

tickets.why: The shared bug-fixer flow: triage, reproduce first, plan approval, and proveRegressionTest.
The FE bug fixer: reproduce on FCP Lab, regression spec, video proof.
The BE bug fixer: a failing Django test first, and an API transcript.
The flaky-test fixer: reproduce with --shuffle seeds, prove 50 green runs, no retries or sleeps.

words.plain: Make the bug happen on purpose, as a test that fails on the current code.
A test that fails while the bug is there and passes once it is fixed, so the bug cannot quietly return.
The main commit the fix started from, where the old code still has the bug.
A second checkout of the same repo in another folder, at another commit.
A test failure before any assertion runs, such as a missing import. It proves nothing about the bug.

review.q: From memory: the two runs of the proof, and what each must show.
review.a: The new test on the base commit with only the test files copied in must fail on an assertion; the same test on the fix must pass.

review.q: What goes on a ticket when the bug fixer cannot reproduce the bug?
review.a: The steps it tried, the seed data and commands it used, what is missing (role, data shape, browser, exact steps) and one specific question. The run ends as handed_off.

remember: Reproduce first: no bug fix counts until its test fails on the old code for a behaviour reason and passes on the fix.
